text:
Things, for being known,

do not stop astonishing us.

The sun is shining,

people in the streets

stroll, eat ice cream;

children run, play,

and there are roses in the courtyards.

As if death were not passing by,

swallowing the streets,

and the Mapocho River were not running

with such strange fish.

Nothing. The sun shines and, as always,

people in the streets.

But a little before curfew

a general stampede breaks

this appearance.

And it is like a cruel relief

to know that they know.

translation.title: The Appearance
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the everyday surface of Chile under curfew and the cruel relief when fear reveals shared knowledge.
